After playing at [[Boston College Eagles basketball|Boston College]] from 2002 to 2006, he was selected by the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] in the [[2006 NBA draft]]. ==High school and college== Smith attended [[Worcester Academy]], a [[University-preparatory school|preparatory school]] in [[Worcester, Massachusetts]], for a year as a [[postgraduate year|postgraduate]] student before college. He went on to score 2,349 points in his collegiate career, placing him second on Boston College's career scoring list (behind [[Troy Bell]]). In his senior season, he had per-game averages of 17.6 points, 9.4 rebounds, 3.0 assists, 1.2 steals, and 0.8 blocked shots.[http://www.bceagles.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/craig_smith_127037.html Craig Smith Bio] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131114003949/http://www.bceagles.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/craig_smith_127037.html |date=2013-11-14 }} ==Professional career== Smith was selected by the Minnesota Timberwolves with the 36th overall pick in the [[2006 NBA draft]]. On August 30, 2006, he signed a multi-year deal with the Timberwolves.{{cite web|url=http://basketball.realgm.com/player/Craig-Smith/Summary/102|title=Craig Smith Player Profile, Portland Trail Blazers, News, Rumors, NBA Stats, NCAA Stats, D-League Stats, International Stats, Game Logs, Bests, Awards|work=RealGM}} Smith averaged 7.4 points and 5.1 rebounds in his rookie year (2006–07) with the Timberwolves. While with the Timberwolves, he earned the nickname "The Rhino" from head coach Kevin McHale for his powerful, charging style of play.{{Cite web |last=Oregonian/OregonLive |first=Jason Quick {{!}} The |date=2012-02-14 |title=A Trail Blazers love story: Craig Smith, "The Rhino," reunites with childhood friend |url=https://www.oregonlive.com/blazers/2012/02/a_trail_blazers_love_story_craig_smith_the_rhino_r.html |access-date=2025-09-18 |website=oregonlive |language=en}} He earned a starting role for the last five games of the season and averaged 12.0 points and 10.2 rebounds while logging an average 34.4 minutes. He had an increased role in the 2007–08 season after a strong rookie performance and a Vegas Summer League performance during which he averaged 21.8 points and 6.0 rebounds. With this performance, Smith earned a spot on the Summer League All-Tournament First Team.{{Cite web |title=NBA Summer League Awards - RealGM |url=https://basketball.realgm.com/nba/summer/1/NBA-Summer-League/7/awards |access-date=2025-09-18 |website=basketball.realgm.com |language=en}} On December 11, 2007, Smith scored 36 points in an 88–102 loss to the [[Washington Wizards]], logging 38 minutes and making 14 of his 22 field goal attempts.{{cite web|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=271211027|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071214144841/http://sports.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=271211027|url-status=dead|archive-date=December 14, 2007|title=Six score in double digits to lift short-handed Wizards|publisher=ESPN}} On July 17, 2008, he re-signed with the Timberwolves on a multi-year deal.{{cite web|url=http://www.insidehoops.com/wolves-resign-smith-071708.shtml|title=Timberwolves re-sign Craig Smith|work=Inside Hoops}} On July 20, 2009, Smith was traded, along with [[Mark Madsen (basketball)|Mark Madsen]] and [[Sebastian Telfair]], to the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] for [[Quentin Richardson]].{{cite web| url=http://www.nba.com/clippers/news/breakingnews090720.html | title=Clippers Acquire Telfair, Smith and Madsen from Minnesota for Richardson | work=NBA.com | date=July 20, 2009 | access-date=July 20, 2009}} On July 19, 2010, Smith re-signed with the Clippers on a one-year deal.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/clippers/news/breakingnews_100719.html|title=CLIPPERS: CLIPPERS REACH DEAL WITH FORWARD CRAIG SMITH|work=nba.com}} On December 15, 2011, Smith signed with the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/2011/news/12/15/blazers-craig-smith.ap/|title=Trail Blazers sign forward Craig Smith|work=NBA.com}} On August 11, 2012, Smith signed with [[Hapoel Jerusalem B.C.|Hapoel Jerusalem]] of Israel for the 2012–13 season.{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/israel/94422/hapoel-jerusalem-signs-former-nba-craig-smith.html|title=Hapoel Jerusalem signs former NBA Craig Smith|date=11 August 2012|work=Sportando}} On March 15, 2013, he was released by Hapoel.{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/israel/99900/hapoel-jerusalem-waive-craig-smith.html|title=Hapoel Jerusalem waive Craig Smith|date=15 March 2013|work=Sportando}} He later joined the [[Shaanxi Wolves|Hong Kong Bulls]] for the 2013 [[National Basketball League (China)|NBL]] season. On March 14, 2014, Smith was acquired by the [[Sioux Falls Skyforce]] of the [[NBA D-League]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/siouxfalls/smith_140314.html|title=NBA Development League: Skyforce Acquires Craig Smith|work=NBA.com}} On September 23, 2014, Smith signed with Israeli club [[Ironi Nes Ziona B.C.|Ironi Nes Ziona]] for the 2014–15 season.{{cite news|title=Former NBA forward Craig Smith inks a deal with Ironi Nes-Ziona|url=https://www.sportando.com/en/europe/israel/135575/former-nba-forward-craig-smith-inks-a-deal-with-ironi-nes-ziona.html|access-date=December 12, 2017|work=Sportando.com|date=September 23, 2014}} In 2019 Craig Smith signed with the Enemies of the Big3. Entering his first season with the BIG3, Craig Smith was selected with the 10th pick in the second round of the 2019 BIG3 draft. ==The Basketball Tournament== Craig Smith played for Team CitiTeam Blazers in the [[The Basketball Tournament 2018|2018]] edition of [[The Basketball Tournament]].
